*sits on the edge of the kang, smoking*

Alright, let me think through this year. I've been doing this 20 years, so I don't need to think too hard about most of it — I just do what works. But you asked, so let me walk through it.

**About my land.** I've got near 380 mu. Most of it's not my own ancestral land — I took over parcels from households whose young people went to the cities. I pay them a yearly rent. That much land, with just four of us in the household, I can't work it alone. My wife and I do what we can, our oldest son helps when he's not driving a truck, and for cotton picking I bring in people from poorer villages — women mostly, paid by the jin they pick.

**Cotton is my main thing.** Around here in western Quzhou, cotton is what we do. The land suits it, and I know it. I'll put cotton on most of my mu — maybe 320 mu. The rest, around 60 mu, is a lower patch that doesn't drain as well and the cotton never does as good there, so I put maize on it. Maize is easier, less work, and I can sell it or feed it.

**Cotton planting.** Late April, after the Qingming cold snap is over. I buy Bt cotton seed from the agro-supply shop in town — the boss tells me what's selling this year, I mostly trust him because I've bought from him ten years running. I don't know the variety names, I just know which packet did well last year.

**Fertilizer for cotton.** I put two bags of compound fertilizer down before planting — that's the base. Then when the cotton starts setting bolls, I topdress with urea, about one bag per mu or a bit less. That works out to, maybe, 15 kg of nitrogen per mu all told? The shop boss told me that number once. I don't count it exactly — I look at the plants. If they're pale I put more, if they're dark green and shooting up too tall I hold back because tall plants don't make bolls.

**Irrigation.** I've got a well. First watering is right after planting to get them up, then once more around flowering if it hasn't rained, and one more at boll-filling if the summer is dry. So two, maybe three waterings. Pumping costs money — the electric meter ticks — so I don't water just because.

**Pesticide.** Cotton needs spraying. Even with Bt seed, I still get aphids and sometimes plant bugs. I spray when I see them, not on a calendar. Also I spray herbicide before the cotton comes up to keep the weeds down, because with this much land I can't hoe it all by hand.

**Picking.** This is the big one. I hire maybe 15-20 women for a few weeks, three picks through September and October. I pay by the jin. This costs me more than the fertilizer.

**Maize on the 60 mu.** Spring maize, planted end of April, same time as the cotton more or less. Regular hybrid seed. One bag of compound at planting, topdress with urea when it's knee-high. Water once or twice. Harvest in September, before I'm too deep into cotton picking. I expect about 450-500 kg/mu — the land there isn't the best but maize forgives it.

**What I worry about.** Cotton prices. They move, and I can't do anything about it. Also if the picking labor gets scarce or expensive, I'm in trouble. And if one of those summer storms comes through at boll-opening, half my cotton is on the ground.
